one_liner: Rust HTML/XML parser with CSS selection for Python; faster than BeautifulSoup4 and html5lib, slower than lxml-based Parsel.
what_it_does: MarkupEver parses HTML/XML into a mutable DOM tree, lets you query it with CSS selectors (soupsieve-compatible syntax, minus some pseudo-classes), and serializes it back to markup, all from a Rust extension exposed to Python via PyO3. It is not a BeautifulSoup drop-in: `parse()`/`parse_file()` return a `TreeDom`/`dom.Document` with its own `select()`/`select_one()` methods, and a separate `Parser.process()` call supports incremental/streaming input instead of mimicking BeautifulSoup's Tag/NavigableString API.
how_it_is_fast: Tokenizing and tree-building run through html5ever (Rust's spec-compliant HTML5 parser) and CSS matching uses servo's `selectors` crate, both compiled natively instead of going through Python's html.parser or the tree BeautifulSoup builds on top. The DOM is a single Vec-backed Rust tree (treedom crate), avoiding per-node Python object churn until a node is touched, and the release build uses fat LTO, one codegen unit, and panic=abort.
when_to_use: Parsing/selecting/serializing many small-to-medium HTML or XML documents from Python where BeautifulSoup4 or html5lib is the measured bottleneck
Need CSS-selector querying (soupsieve-style syntax) without switching to XPath
Building a DOM from scratch and serializing it (e.g. generating HTML), not just parsing existing markup
Large or streamed input where incremental parsing via Parser.process() avoids buffering the whole document
Deploying to Linux, Windows, or macOS with a prebuilt PyPI wheel - no local Rust toolchain needed
when_not_to_use: You already call lxml/Parsel directly - on the project's own benchmark table, Parsel beats MarkupEver on every measured operation (parse, select, serialize)
You need the CSS :has() pseudo-class - an open issue says it does not work
You need a BeautifulSoup-compatible API (Tag, NavigableString, .find()) - MarkupEver's dom/select API is different, so adopting it is a rewrite, not a swap

You need airtight cross-thread sharing of parser objects - an unsound `impl Sync` on Tendril-based parser/matching types was reported (issue #10) and fixed later, but the exact fixed version is not documented
You want independently reproduced numbers - only the maintainer's own benchmark exists, with no published benchmark code, no stated Python version, and no stated build flags

integration.dependencies: Rust build deps only (pyo3 0.29, parking_lot 0.12, hashbrown 0.17, plus html5ever/selectors pulled in via the treedom and matching workspace crates); Python runtime has no extra dependencies
integration.min_toolchain: Rust edition 2021 (build-time only, via maturin); Python >=3.8, with wheels published for CPython 3.9-3.14 and PyPy - no Rust toolchain needed to install from PyPI
integration.platforms: Linux, Windows, macOS per PyPI classifiers; benchmarked on x86-64 (Manjaro), no documented architecture restriction
integration.thread_safety: README claims 'completely thread-safe', but issue #10 found the `impl Sync` on Tendril-based parser/matching types unsound (non-atomic refcount under concurrent access); addressed by later 'remove unsafe blocks' PRs, exact fixed version not documented
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — explain: same parse -> select -> serialize workflow as BeautifulSoup4, but a different, non-object-compatible API (TreeDom/dom.Document, select()/select_one())

gotchas: CSS :has() pseudo-class does not work (open issue, unresolved as of this session)
Historical unsound Sync impl on parser/matching types tied to html5ever's Tendril type (issue #10) - fixed later, but pin a recent version if you share parser objects across threads
A separate 'attaching a node to itself causes crash' bug was reported and closed - confirm you're past that fix
pyproject.toml's PyPI classifier lists the license as MIT while the actual LICENSE file and Cargo.toml both say MPL-2.0 - a metadata inconsistency, not an alternate license grant
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick MarkupEver over html5-parser when you also want CSS selection and DOM construction/serialization in the same library, not just fast HTML5-to-lxml-tree parsing; pick selectolax or Parsel/lxml directly instead when you don't need MarkupEver's DOM-building API, since both outperform MarkupEver on this same class of parse/select/serialize benchmark.
verified_claims_summary: On the maintainer's own micro-benchmark (Manjaro Linux x86_64, 8GB RAM, Intel i3-1115G4; Python version and compiler flags unstated), MarkupEver parsed a test HTML page in 4,927us avg vs BeautifulSoup4(lxml)'s 22,809us (~4.6x) and html5lib's 63,489us; CSS-selected in 310us vs BeautifulSoup4's 2,995us (~9.7x); and serialized in 1,952us vs BeautifulSoup4's 14,900us (~7.6x). On the same table, Parsel (using lxml/libxml2 directly) beat MarkupEver on all three operations (4,072us parse, 161us select, 1,276us serialize).
status_note: Actively maintained (last commit 2026-07-21, CI running on push) and MPL-2.0 licensed, but it's a compiled PyO3/maturin extension rather than a source-drop, and it's a small, largely single-author project (37 stars) with an unresolved CSS-selector gap and a past thread-safety soundness bug, so treat it as promising but young.
